one_liner: Manage hospital housekeeping and infection-prevention cleaning at the NIH Clinical Center in Bethesda, mainly by overseeing the environmental services contractor as its COR.
fit_summary: This GS-13 role requires a year of GS-12-level experience in clinical environmental services quality assurance, clinical-setting procurement, and writing statements of work and sole source justifications. Nothing on file shows Daniel has hospital or contract-administration experience, though IEM consulting may include some contractor oversight or stakeholder work. Daniel's policy knowledge and people skills are not central to this position.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens), plus military spouse and individuals with disabilities hiring paths; no federal status is required.

Specialized experience: at least one year equivalent to GS-12 in clinical environmental services QA, process improvement, clinical procurement, SOW/evaluation criteria/sole source preparation, and stakeholder guidance.
Security/suitability listed as 'Other'; expect a background investigation and possibly medical or physical requirements for a hospital setting.
The COR Level III role implies you must hold or obtain FAC-COR Level III certification; confirm this with HR.
strategy: The application window is only October 26–30, 2026, so draft your two-page resume and preview the questionnaire at the linked USA Staffing URL before the posting opens.
Answer the questionnaire honestly. Rate yourself 'expert' only where your resume shows clear evidence, because overstating can get you removed and references may be checked.

If your IEM work involved writing SOWs, evaluating proposals, monitoring contractor performance, or supporting public-health or hospital clients, describe it concretely in your own words with dates and hours per week.
Do not copy announcement language. Match the keywords with specific actions you actually performed.
Realistically, treat this as a low-odds application. Prioritize emergency management, FEMA, or legislative and public-affairs roles at GS-9 to GS-12, which fit your background better.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client] on [disaster recovery/preparedness project] at IEM, drafting [statements of work/evaluation criteria] for [number/type] of contracted services worth [$ amount]. ([dates], [hours]/week)
Monitored contractor performance against [metrics/standards] for [program], documenting deficiencies and coordinating corrective actions with [client agency stakeholders].
Served as primary liaison between [client agency] and [internal/external stakeholders], providing technical guidance on [topic] to [number] of partners.
interview_questions: How have you used quality assurance surveillance to hold a services contractor accountable?
Walk us through preparing a statement of work or sole source justification.
How would you keep patient bed turnover and cleaning on schedule during a staffing shortage or infection outbreak?
Describe a time you resolved a conflict between a contractor and internal stakeholders.
watch_outs: Five-day open period: missing October 30 ends your chance.
The requirement for clinical or hospital environmental services experience is very specific and likely disqualifying without it.
On-site only in Bethesda, MD, with no telework, which means a long commute from Manassas.
COR Level III certification is likely expected; verify whether you can obtain it after hire.
